newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem leader Nur Misuari has discounted threats by a new group, led by his former top general, which has vowed to mount attacks to sabotage his peace deal with the Philippine government. Misuari said the new group called the Moro Islamic Liberation Organisation (MILO) has "only a handful of followers". (MANILA BULLETIN)
- At least 15 people were reported missing and feared dead when heavy rains triggered a landslide on Tuesday in a gold mine site at Mt. Mambitayan, a known gold rush area. (MALAYA)
- Eighty seven people, 23 of whom are foreigners who are mostly Chinese nationals, are facing the death penalty under the new Heinous Crimes Act for drug trafficking. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Higher dollar inflows from investors and Filipino overseas contract workers have sent the country's balance of payments soaring to a surplus of $3.995 billion during the first eight months of the year, up 291 percent over the $1.02 billion surplus registered during the same period in 1995. (TODAY)
- Despite continued intervention by the Central Bank, the peso tumbled anew against the dollar on Tuesday falling to 26.245 from 26.238 the previous day. (TODAY)
- Westmont Bank has formalized its takeover of Zipporah Mining & Industrial Corp after its President Edgardo Espiritu was elected chairman of the latter. (TODAY)

- U.S. investment firm Goldman Sachs raised its 1996 gross national product forecast for the Philippines to seven percent from 6.1 percent. It said the adjustment was based on anticipated strong flows of money from abroad. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Despite the strong performance of the stock market, most initial public offerings so far this year have been disappointing. Six of 10 companies that went public this year were trading below their offering price. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
